edits.modify_to: (3) go through EVERY container frame after the first one, in order, up to and including the last demonstration frame, and label each frame before doing anything else: either 'all at slots' or 'slots P and Q empty'. A listed position within a few pixels of a slot (e.g. [98, 153] for [99, 155]) is AT that slot; a frame in which two listed positions match no slot (containers in mid-swing at intermediate positions, e.g. [73, 140] and [101, 139] where the slots are [71, 123] and [103, 159]) is an 'empty' frame for the two slots nobody occupies in it. Listed positions carry no identity: a container can only be followed through slots, never by matching positions in the last frame to positions in the first.

edits.modify_from: if the table and the parity disagree, recount the runs. Shuffles of pairs the named container is not in do not change its slot;
edits.modify_to: if the table and the parity disagree, recount the runs. Shuffles of pairs the named container is not in do not change its slot. The entry may only be written AFTER these four things have actually been written out in the answer: the frame-by-frame labels, the numbered list of shuffles, the slot table after each swap, and the parity check; a block of one or more consecutive 'empty' frames is one shuffle even when it is the only shuffle in the video. Whenever a shuffle empties the named container's own slot, the named container ends at the OTHER slot of that pair; so if its slot was emptied an odd number of times the entry must differ from the container that first sat over the cube. Every demonstration of this task contains at least one shuffle: an answer that finds zero shuffles, or that returns every named cube to its first container, has mislabelled frames and must be recounted;

edits.modify_to: Worked example (two cubes, two different pairs each shuffle once, so BOTH named containers move): green cube at [92, 156], blue cube at [125, 117]; first container frame lists [80, 121], [89, 157], [123, 116], [131, 154]; green's slot is [89, 157], blue's is [123, 116]; frames 80-96 list two positions matching no slot while [123, 116] and [131, 154] stay, so 'slots [80, 121] and [89, 157] empty'; frame 112 'all at slots'; frames 128-160 'slots [123, 116] and [131, 154] empty'; last frame 'all at slots'. Shuffle 1 swaps [80, 121] and [89, 157]: green now at [80, 121]. Shuffle 2 swaps [123, 116] and [131, 154]: blue now at [131, 154]. Last frame lists those slots as [82, 121] and [131, 154]; entry [[82, 121], [131, 154]].
